title: Extract RepoPact Core and Independent Workbench

preflight.note: Registered from the operator-approved WI074 specification before implementation began. Physical extraction, repository creation, publication, and destructive migration have not begun and are not authorized by this proposal.

acceptance_criteria.text: Preserve: Independently verify complete extraction-source backups, refs, tags and reachable objects. Record local WI072, divergent history and GitHub-hosted metadata limitations.
Manifest: Produce a complete source-to-destination mapping by path, crate and command, with source revision, destination ownership and no unexplained omissions.
Architecture: Obtain approval of the architectural decisions governing Rust distribution, public interfaces, optional functionality, release identity and cross-repository governance.
Core build: Build the extracted core's wheel, source distribution and Rust engine from a clean standalone checkout without Workbench.
CLI compatibility: Preserve all documented stable 3.1.3 headless commands or explicitly authorize and version changes.
Install identity: Preserve the `repopact` PyPI and CLI names, matching engine identity and fail-closed protocol compatibility.
Semantic singularity: Establish and verify that core alone owns canonical validation, governance interpretation, graph semantics and mutation.
Rust consumption: Prove Workbench can build against exact immutable core Rust dependencies without original-monorepo path references.
GUI runtime: Prove desktop Workbench and Android do not require a Python interpreter or pip installation at runtime.
Feature parity: Pass contract tests for desktop APIs, repository sessions, watchers, mutation preview/apply, graph queries, Tauri commands and generated frontend types.
Native platforms: Produce repeatable native Windows/Linux and supported Android evidence. Bound macOS/iOS claims to actual testing.
Admission correctness: Preserve shipped headless admission and guard functionality, security boundaries, feature gates and accurate assurance classifications.
Authentication and secrets: Keep optional GitHub integration and platform credential storage separate from core semantics, with no secrets leaked to frontend code, logs or build artifacts.
Conformance: Pass the frozen 3.1.3 conformance fixture oracle and coverage checks against the extracted core, including diagnostic identity and Python regression comparison.
Reproducibility: Verify independent clean source exports, artifact identity, wheel contents, native binary provenance and explicitly documented platform normalization.
Release independence: Establish separate core/Workbench versions, a tested compatibility matrix, offline clean-clone installation, upgrade and rollback procedures.

Governance continuity: Preserve authoritative decisions, evidence, licenses, historical work items and frozen-surface constraints with a traceable migration manifest and no fabricated timestamps or duplicate authorities.
Proving Ground: Preserve historical research evidence and have new benchmark runs install explicitly pinned core releases.
ForgeWire adopter: Maintain ForgeWire's existing RepoPact integration until a compatible release is independently validated and its adoption separately authorized.

Documentation: Update installation, architecture, contributor, API/CLI, configuration, platform, security, release, migration and support documentation. Regenerate derived views from authoritative records.

Financial and remote safety: Do not create repositories, enable workflows, invoke paid services, push unapproved changes, publish releases, delete original refs or change global developer environments without the appropriate authorization.
Rollback: Document and exercise rollback from verified backups and independently built artifacts, including unavailable-remote and incompatible-version scenarios.
CI policy: Preserve local-first validation as authoritative. Hosted CI must remain optional and cost-controlled.

Evidence closeout: Link every satisfied acceptance criterion to immutable evidence recording real commands, environment, revision, scope, result and limitations. Never claim completion from planned tests or unverified assertions.
